hook: The Bengali poet who was the first non-European Nobel winner, and wrote two national anthems.

pages.x: Rabindranath Tagore was born in Calcutta in 1861, the youngest of 13 children in a rich and gifted Bengali family. He hated school and was taught at home. He wrote his first poems at eight.
In 1878 he was sent to England to become a lawyer. He left without a degree, but came home in love with English books and Irish and Scottish songs.
In the 1890s he ran his family's estates in the countryside of Bengal, living on a houseboat on the river Padma, and wrote short stories about the villagers he met.
In 1901 he started a school at Santiniketan where classes were held outdoors, under the trees. It grew into a university, Visva-Bharati.
His book of poems Gitanjali, "Song Offerings", which he translated into English himself, won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913. He was the first person from outside Europe to win a Nobel Prize.
He wrote more than 2,000 songs. Two of them became the national anthems of India and of Bangladesh, and the writer of Sri Lanka's anthem was his student. This is India's anthem, Jana Gana Mana.
The British knighted him in 1915. In 1919, after British troops shot hundreds of unarmed people at Amritsar, he gave the knighthood back in protest.
He is said to have given Gandhi the name Mahatma, "great soul". In 1930 he met Albert Einstein near Berlin, and the two argued about whether truth and beauty exist without people to see them.
In old age he began to doodle on his manuscripts, and the doodles became paintings. He made more than 2,000 pictures, shown in Paris, Moscow and New York.
Tagore reshaped the literature and music of Bengal, was the first Nobel winner from outside Europe, and his songs are sung by two nations.
pts: First Nobel Prize winner from outside Europe
Wrote the national anthems of India and Bangladesh
